ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #9
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.

2. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.

3. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.

4. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.

5. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. run
   C. quickly
   D. blue

6. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.

7. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. goed
   C. went
   D. going

8. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.

9. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. No full stops
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

10. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.

11. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the library

12. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 6.1.2 Speaking Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Word Classes and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Clauses: and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

====

2. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.

3. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.

4. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.

5. B — run

6. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.

7. C — went

8. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.

9. D — One main idea with supporting sentences

10. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.

11. B — Where is the library?

12. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 6.1.2 Speaking Fluency; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Word Classes; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Clauses:; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
